prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "tech_docs", with the standing line "The developer's guide to a desktop poetry dictionary — Go services, an embedded database, and a React window." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows A left-to-right cutaway of one desktop application. At far left, an embedded database file drawn as a stack of two joined tables, one of word entries and one of pointer rows between entries. A pipe of raw definition text leaves it and enters three stacked Go service blocks: one for entries, one for speech, one for images. Below them the parser is drawn as a small comb that splits a run of raw text into ordered boxes — segments — each segment holding smaller tokens, one of which is shaded as a clickable cross-reference. The parsed structure passes through a narrow bridge wall between Go and JavaScript, then into a webview window at right showing a rendered definition with underlined cross-references. A return arrow from the window back to the services carries a search query and a requested entry.

Magnified circles set beside it show Circle one, a curly tag inside a sentence of raw text becoming an underlined clickable cross-reference in the rendered window. Circle two, a typed keyword striking a virtual index table, which returns matching row numbers that are joined back to the full entry record. Circle three, one pointer row drawn as an arrow from a source entry to a destination entry, making a directed graph of entries. Circle four, a definition sent to the speech service and returning as an audio file stored in a cache folder beside the database.

Colour is used so that Warm ochre marks raw stored text before parsing. Deep teal marks structured, parsed output crossing the bridge. Muted red marks search and the links between entries. Grey marks generated artefacts, audio and images, held in cache.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: four documents in tech_docs; three core services; three segment types, text, quote and poem; two token types; six routes; three full-text indexes.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: items, links, ItemsService, FTS5, Wails, {word: poetry}, segments, tokens, parser, migrations, bindings, startup, shutdown, Dashboard, Search, Item detail, Settings, Reports, Tables, Command palette.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: SQLite, items, links, ItemsService, speech service, images service, parser, segments, tokens, Wails, React window {word: poetry}, reference token, FTS5, audio cache Architecture, Data Modeling, Backend Services, Frontend Dashboard, Search, Item detail, Settings, Reports, Tables, Command palette startup, migrations, bindings, shutdown

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Definitions are stored as raw tagged text; Services are Go methods the window can call; Parsing happens before anything reaches the window Tags become links to other entries; Index tables rank matches, then rejoin records; Audio and images are generated once, reused Four documents cover the whole system Six routes share one sidebar layout Startup opens the database, then builds services
